newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-BHP to upgrade NZ steel plant - paper.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-BHP to upgrade NZ steel plant - paper.

text.p: The Broken Hill Pty Co (BHP) Ltd would spend NZ$27 million to rebuild the number one melter at BHP Steel's New Zealand steelworks, The Australian newspaper reported on Wednesday.
"BHP has committed to an upgrade of its troubled New Zealand steelworks after local management implemented big job cuts and committed to cut costs by NZ$50 million a year," the Australian said.

"The managing director of BHP NZ Steel, Malcolm Burns, said management had so far cut 250 jobs from its 1,630 workforce by offering voluntary redundancy packages, and had committed to slicing a further 150 before May 31," the newspaper said.
Burns warned he would need to cut another 200 jobs at Glenbrook beyond May 31 this year, to reach an optimum workforce of 1,000, The Australian said.
Burns also said the future of the operation was under threat from the strengthening New Zealand dollar.
"If it keeps strengthening, it gets to a point where it's impossible to keep driving costs down," Burns was quoted as saying by the newspaper.
BHP NZ Steel exports about 60 percent of its 750,000 tonnes a year production.
BHP NZ Steel said in August last year that BHP was considering options for the New Zealand mill at Glenbrook south of Auckland which could involve halving production.
It said then it needed BHP's approval to rebuild melter number one if it was to continue full production.
